newsitem.title: MACAU: China shouldn't run HK like zone--Portugal's Silva.
newsitem.headline: China shouldn't run HK like zone--Portugal's Silva.

text.p: Former Portuguese prime minister Anibal Cavaco Silva has said China should not try to run Hong Kong affairs as it handled its own Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in China.
Hong Kong, ceasing to be a British colony, becomes an autonomous Special Administrative Region of China at a midnight ceremony on Monday.

"The methods of administration in Shenzhen (SEZ) and Zhuhai (SEZ) must not be duplicated in Hong Kong and Macau, which have very different ways of life," said Silva, who will be present when Britain's Prince Charles formally hands Hong Kong back to Chinese President Jiang Zemin after 156 years of British rule.
Under a one country-two systems agreement hammered out in 1984, Hong Kong will have a considerable degree of autonomy.
"Macau and Hong Kong need autonomy within the framework of liberties, rights and (legal) guarantees," Silva told Reuters.
But Silva said he expected existing administrative frameworks to be maintained in both Hong Kong and Macau after they revert to Chinese sovereignty.
After Hong Kong's handover later on Monday, Macau will be the only part of China still under foreign rule.
Macau reverts to Chinese rule in 1999 under the terms of the 1987 Sino-Portuguese agreement, which Silva signed with then Chinese premier Zhao Zhiyang.
